stories.summary: Evan Vucci/REUTERS Donald Trump has lost his macho status among young male voters. articles.author: Laura C. Morel
articles.summary: One of the many Democrats who flipped state House seats during the historic midterms was a public school teacher in Florida’s Palm Beach County. Elizabeth Holmes hadn’t even considered politics before 2026, and within months, she unseated Meg Weinberger, a Donald Trump–endorsed Republican known as “MAGA Meg” who had won the seat in 2024. Earlier this year, Weinberger sponsored legislation to rename the Palm Beach airport after the president, a project that cost $5.5 million . Holmes’ win there highlights how the MAGA movement is losing some of its power—even in the county Trump calls home. The genesis of Holmes’ dizzyingly rapid campaign and victory can be traced back to April 15, an especially hard day at work. One of Holmes’ special education students ended up in the hospital after a mental health crisis. When Holmes got home later that day, she saw the news that during union contract negotiations, the superintendent offered the district’s teachers a 1.5 percent raise—a far cry from the 3.5 percent they’d been hoping for.
